text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#HD-9123 - GPU kernel OOM surge detected in us-west-2/gpu-pool-7. Error rate spike on cuda-kernel-alloc (5xxs).

pagerduty: Incident HD-9123 created and routed to on-call. Priority: high. Paging alex_oncall.

alex_oncall: ACK. I'm on it. Can someone paste the alert log?

maya_sre: copying recent container logs — looks like repeated kernel allocation failures followed by driver resets. Short logs:
```
[2026-03-14T18:21:02Z] cuda: alloc failed: out of memory (size=268435456)
[2026-03-14T18:21:02Z] kernel: evicting kv-cache for model: redwood-tiny-v1
[2026-03-14T18:21:03Z] driver: GPU reset triggered
```

alex_oncall: thx. Any customer-facing errors?

jordan_support: seeing a handful of customers in us-west-2 reporting 503/timeouts for embed endpoints since ~18:20. Correlates with spike in errors. Customer IDs: cust-1045, cust-7782 (high priority).

ryan_eng: rolling window shows a surge in peak seq-lengths and batch sizes at 18:19 -> ~20% more KV cache usage than normal. Likely filling GPU mem.

liz_infra: autoscaler hasn't kicked due to pod CPU thresholds not tripped; it's memory pressure on GPU, not CPU. We can evict caches or spin new nodes manually.

alex_oncall: quick mitigation ideas: 1) enable aggressive kv-cache eviction on affected model processes, 2) reduce max batch size via live route config, 3) trigger emergency pool-scale (add two nodes), 4) fallback to quantized model variant. Which should we do first?

maya_sre: prioritize eviction + reduce batch size — fastest. I'll push a config to evict less-recent prefixes and apply batch cap. If still failing, trigger scale.

ryan_eng: +1. I'll prepare config snippets. Proposed route change: cap batch_size to 4 and max_seq to 1024 for the redwood-tiny-v1 route in us-west-2.

alex_oncall: go for it. @maya_sre, can you run the eviction command? Also ping infra to pre-warm nodes.

maya_sre: running eviction now. Command:
```bash
infractl gpu-kvcache evict --pool us-west-2/gpu-pool-7 --models redwood-tiny-v1 --age 5m
```

maya_sre: eviction completed, saw ~18% reclaimed memory across nodes.

liz_infra: pre-warming two nodes now. Added nodes to pool (request id: prewarm-175888). ETA ~120s.

jordan_support: customers cust-1045 and cust-7782 acknowledged loss of service; opened support tickets and notified account owners. No data exposure.

alex_oncall: applying batch cap change to routing config for the route. Patch applied and rolled to 3/3 routers in us-west-2.

ryan_eng: adding fallback rule to route to quantized-variant if GPU alloc fails 3x in 30s. Pushing now.

pagerduty: user alex_oncall acknowledged incident HD-9123 at 2026-03-14T18:23:45Z.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: mitigation steps in progress: kvcache eviction done, batch cap rolled, pre-warm started, fallback rule pushed. Monitoring for error rate reduction.

maya_sre: monitoring metrics — kernel-alloc errors dropping from 120/min -> 18/min in last 4 minutes. Latency for affected endpoints improving, error rate down to ~1.2% from 8%.

alex_oncall: good. @jordan_support keep customers updated that a mitigation was applied and we're watching. I'll hold the page until we see sustained stability 10m.

jordan_support: will update tickets and set ETA to 30m for follow-up.

liz_infra: pre-warm nodes are ready and joined pool. No further scale needed for now.

ryan_eng: plan for follow-up: root-cause likely combo of sudden seq-length/batch spike + insufficient kvcache eviction heuristics. Filing follow-up RFC for improved memory throttling and autoscaler hooks.

alex_oncall: marking incident as acknowledged and monitoring. If error rate stays <2% for 10m, we'll resolve. Otherwise escalate to on-call escalation policy.

pagerduty: Incident HD-9123 status: acknowledged by alex_oncall.

incident-bot: :hourglass_flowing_sand: follow-up checklist: 1) include timeline in postmortem, 2) attach config diffs for eviction + route cap, 3) schedule runbook update for kvcache eviction thresholds. Assigned: maya_sre, ryan_eng.

maya_sre: noted, will draft the timeline.

alex_oncall: thanks everyone. keeping thread pinned. :thumbsup:

(End of thread)
